question: What does the term ‘Overdraft’ mean in banking?

options.text: The process of transferring funds between bank accounts
The maximum withdrawal limit from an ATM

solution:
The correct answer is __**Short-term financing facility**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Short-term financing facility** is what the term 'Overdraft' means in banking.
 
• An overdraft allows an account holder to withdraw more money than what is available in their bank account.
 
• It is a type of short-term loan provided by banks to help cover temporary cash shortfalls.
 
• The bank charges interest on the overdrawn amount, and there may also be fees associated with the overdraft facility.
 
• Overdrafts are useful for managing cash flow and unexpected expenses, ensuring that transactions are not declined due to insufficient funds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The interest rate on an overdraft can be higher compared to other types of loans.
 
• Overdraft limits are typically set by the bank based on the customer's creditworthiness and account history.
 
• Exceeding the overdraft limit can result in additional penalties and higher interest rates.
 
• It is important for account holders to monitor their account balances regularly to avoid excessive overdraft fees.
 
• Some banks offer overdraft protection services, which link the primary account to another account or line of credit to cover overdrafts.
